mappings.note: Both contain the title 'To the choirmaster', 'Do not destroy' (Al-Thascheth/Ødelegg ikke), and attribution to David.
Both ask if the mighty speak righteously and judge with integrity.
Both describe practicing injustice in the heart and weighing out violence on earth.
Both state the wicked go astray from birth/womb and are liars.
Both compare their poison to a serpent's and describe them as deaf snakes closing their ears.
Both mention not listening to charmers or the skilled enchanter.
Both call on God/Eternal to break teeth and jaws of lions/lion cubs.
Both describe flowing away like water and arrows being broken when the bow is drawn.
Both compare them to a melting snail and a stillborn child that never sees the sun.

The translation says 'the wind will carry them away' (le vent les emportera), whereas the OSMAIN text says 'he shall sweep them away' (skal han feie dem bort). The agent of action differs slightly, but the core imagery is the same. However, looking closely at the end of v10 in OSMAIN: 'både det rå og det brennende' (both raw and burning) vs Translation 'vertes ou enflammées'. This is a match. Wait, let's re-read carefully. 
OSMAIN v10: 'Før deres gryter kjenner varmen fra tornekrattet, skal han feie dem bort, både det rå og det brennende.'
Translation v10: 'Avant que vos chaudières aient senti le feu des épines, vertes ou enflammées, le vent les emportera.'
The content is effectively the same. The match type is 'exact' in terms of meaning, though the agent changes from 'he' to 'the wind'. I will classify as 'exact' as no significant text is missing or added that changes the verse count logic.

The OSMAIN v11 contains two sentences: 'Den rettferdige skal glede seg...' AND 'Og mennesker skal si...'. The Translation v11 only contains the first sentence ('Le juste se réjouira...'). The second sentence of OSMAIN is missing in this translation verse.
This verse contains the second half of OSMAIN v11 ('Et l'on dira: Oui...'). The OSMAIN text for v11 was split into two translation verses (v11 and v12).
